meta.title: OBJECTSCADA - Industrial control and monitoring system
meta.description: OBJECTSCADA is a modern web-based SCADA platform for industrial monitoring, control, and automation of technological processes. Supports Siemens S7, Modbus, MQTT, OPC UA, EtherNet/IP.

hero.sub: Monitoring, control and automation of technological processes in real time. Supports all major PLC protocols, visual circuit editor and built-in AI assistant.

features.intro: Full-featured SCADA platform with a single interface for monitoring, controlling and analyzing technological processes.

items.title: Real-time monitoring
items.description: WebSocket connection provides instant data update. TimescaleDB stores time series with nanosecond precision.

items.title: Visual schematic editor
items.description: Drag-and-drop flow chart editor based on Konva.js. Create interactive mimic diagrams with animation of device states.

items.title: Accident management
items.description: Multi-level alarm system with priorities. Event log, acknowledgment, escalation of notifications. History of emergency situations.

items.title: Trends and data history
items.description: Plotting historical data graphs with scaling. Export to Excel, CSV. Comparison of several parameters on one graph.

items.title: Sequences and recipes
items.description: Visual programming of technological sequences. Management of recipes, stages and batches (batch automation).

items.title: Role-based access model
items.description: Flexible RBAC system: operators, engineers, administrators. User activity log. JWT authentication.

items.title: Multilingual interface
items.description: Full localization via i18next. RTL (Arabic) support. Switch language without reloading the page.

items.title: Docker deployment
items.description: Full containerization via Docker Compose. One file - the entire stack: backend, frontend, database, Redis, PLC worker.

integrations.intro: Connect any industrial equipment without modification - the system supports standard protocols out of the box.

protocols.name: Siemens S7
protocols.subtitle: Snap7 + TIA Openness
protocols.description: Full support for S7-300/400/1200/1500. Read/write variables DB, M, I, Q. Integration with TIA Portal for automatic configuration deployment.

protocols.name: Modbus
protocols.subtitle: RTU / TCP / ASCII
protocols.description: Modbus RTU via RS-485/RS-232 and Modbus TCP/IP. Supports all function codes: Coils, Discrete Inputs, Holding Registers, Input Registers.

protocols.name: MQTT
protocols.subtitle: Broker / Client
protocols.description: IoT device protocol. Subscribe to topics, publish commands. Compatible with Mosquitto, HiveMQ, AWS IoT Core. QoS 0/1/2.

protocols.name: OPC UA
protocols.subtitle: Client / Server
protocols.description: Industry standard IIoT. Secure data exchange with any OPC UA-compatible equipment. Support Node ID, Browse, Subscription.

protocols.name: EtherNet/IP
protocols.subtitle: Allen-Bradley / Rockwell
protocols.description: CIP protocol for Allen-Bradley PLCs. Supports ControlLogix, CompactLogix, MicroLogix. Tag reading, diagnostics.

tia.title: TIA Portal Agent (.NET)
tia.body: The Agent for Windows automatically exports the variable configuration from the Siemens TIA Portal project to the SCADA system. One-button tag synchronization—no manual data entry.

ai.intro: The RAG assistant based on FastAPI and Qdrant analyzes your production data and answers questions about equipment, accidents and processes in real time.
capabilities: Answers to questions about the condition of equipment

messages.text: What is the average temperature of the R-201 reactor over the last 24 hours?
The average temperature of the R-201 reactor over the last 24 hours was **82.4°C**. Maximum value: 91.2°C at 14:32, minimum: 74.8°C at 03:15. No deviations from the norm were recorded.
Was pump P-101 in trouble this week?

Pump P-101 was stopped due to an accident **1 time** - on April 12 at 09:47. Cause: bearing overheating (temperature 78°C at set point 75°C). The accident was acknowledged by operator Ivanov I.I. at 09:52, pump restarted at 10:05.

architecture.intro: Each component is optimized for its task - from the UI to the highly loaded Rust worker that works directly with the hardware.

cards.title: Programs
cards.desc: Automation scenarios — sequences and recipes: start, steps, execution status, binding to lines and areas

cards.title: PLCs
cards.desc: Controllers: connection, link status, data exchange settings (Modbus, OPC UA, etc.)

cards.title: I/O points
cards.desc: Physical inputs/outputs: addressing and signal binding

cards.title: Devices
cards.desc: Plant objects (pumps, valves, PID, etc.): parameters, modes, binding to I/O and diagrams

cards.title: Roles

cards.title: Settings
cards.desc: General application parameters, license, system information

versusClassic.intro: Five practical differences between our web platform and traditional client SCADA.

items.desc: Via browser — no separate client needed, unified UX on any device.
Python + React/TypeScript — open source, easy to find developers and integrate custom logic.
API-first and WebSocket — MES, ERP, cloud, analytics without additional middleware.
Docker containers — reproducible environments, predictable deployment, simple maintenance.
Modbus/OPC UA + code export for Siemens — minimal gap between the SCADA project and the controller code.
